core_obligations: Parts (1) and (3) (proof lines 21236-21247): choose a K-injective complex of abelian sheaves representing K; the injectivity comparison together with the defining equation of the comparison (for part (1)) and with the cartesian diagram of topologies (for part (3)) gives the identities.
Parts (5) and (6) (proof lines 21249-21254): these are the two localisation statements for cartesian squares, one for sheaves of abelian groups and one for modules.

Parts (2) (proof lines 21256-21262): the pushforwards along the morphisms of ringed sites are compared through the composition lemma Rpi_{S,*} o Rf_big,* = Rf_small,* o Rpi_{T,*}, and since the restriction functors are exact the conclusion follows.
Part (4) (proof lines 21264-21267): part (6) together with part (2) applied to the base changed morphism gives the module statement.
proof_roadmap: Compute the abelian statements with K-injective representatives and the injectivity comparison.
Quote the two localisation statements for cartesian squares.
Compare the ringed pushforwards through the composition lemma and exactness of the restrictions, and deduce the remaining module statement from the base changed case.
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares the big and small pushforwards for a morphism of schemes, in six forms covering abelian sheaves, modules, restriction to the small site of a base, and base change of the comparison (statement lines 21195-21233). The proof (proof lines 21235-21267) uses K-injective representatives and the injectivity comparison for the abelian statements, quotes the two localisation statements for cartesian squares, and obtains the module statements through the composition lemma for ringed pushforwards together with exactness of the restrictions. H2: a collection of short reductions, each written out.
